input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: The wrapper now reuses one shared statistics dict across all calls to the same decorated function and clears it on each call, instead of giving each call its own dict. Concurrent or re-entrant calls on different threads then clear and overwrite each other's statistics.
- rationale: Trigger: two threads call the same @retry-decorated function at the same time, or the function calls itself recursively. Each call runs stats.clear() on the same dict and the copy writes attempt counts into it, so one call's statistics are reset or mixed with another's. Impact: retry statistics read by callers are silently wrong, and the original per-call copy design that guarded against this is lost.
critique: The finding names the same mechanism: a single shared stats dict is cleared and reused on every call. Concurrent threads or recursive calls therefore wipe and mix each other's statistics. This matches the labeled root cause and failure path.
